Training is provided on key topics (Internal Audit, Fraud, Treasury, Risk) but is not based on a structured assessment of what capabilities the committee actually needs.
findings.matters: If committee members lack expertise in treasury management, accounting standards, or pensions liability, they cannot effectively challenge management on complex financial matters or spot emerging problems. This weakens the council's financial governance.

This gap means the committee may not be fully aware of audit concerns or control issues.
findings.matters: Private auditor meetings are where auditors escalate financial control problems that they cannot easily raise in public. Without them, governance weaknesses or financial risks could remain hidden from leadership and therefore from lenders assessing the council's financial health.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - External Auditors Audit Plan 2025/26
findings.headline: Multiple significant risks in high-value asset and pension valuations with material estimation uncertainty
findings.detail: Identified as significant risks: land and buildings valuation (rolling five-year revaluation with indexation), investment property valuations (full annual revaluation), and defined benefit pension net liability (IAS 19). All assessed as high inherent risk, involve external RICS valuers or actuaries, and are sensitive to changes in key assumptions (discount rates, inflation, mortality, market conditions).
findings.matters: Large material balances involving high subjective estimation create audit complexity, potential for material misstatement, and balance sheet volatility that affects financial position assessment.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - External Auditors Audit Plan 2025/26
findings.headline: Statutory backstop date 31 January 2027: further disclaimer likely if audit procedures incomplete
findings.detail: The Code of Audit Practice 2024 requires auditors to issue their report by the backstop date even if audit procedures are incomplete, which will result in a disclaimer of opinion. This is the fourth consecutive year operating under backstop deadlines. Auditors acknowledge significant additional work is required to build back assurance.
findings.matters: Even if the council meets the 31 January 2027 deadline, a further disclaimer opinion will be issued if audit work cannot be completed, perpetuating lack of audit assurance and credit uncertainty.

findings.quote: The Code of Audit Practice 2024 specifies that auditors are required to issue their auditor's report before these dates, even if planned audit procedures are not fully complete, so that local government bodies can comply with the statutory reporting deadline. Where audit work is not complete, this will give rise to a disclaimer of opinion.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - External Auditors Audit Plan 2025/26

This has not been subject to audit procedures in previous years. If occurring, it would understate revenue expenditure and overstate property, plant and equipment additions.
findings.matters: Systematic misclassification of revenue as capital expenditure distorts the reported revenue budget position and overstates the capital asset base, potentially masking deteriorating revenue sustainability.

findings.matters: Inability to produce timely, compliant financial statements on the first attempt raises questions about control environment, financial reporting reliability, and management capability that lenders depend on for credit decisions.

findings.quote: There are significant weaknesses in the Council's arrangements for the preparation and publication of financial statements. findings.paper_title: Appendix A - External Auditors Audit Plan 2025/26

Recovery targeted for 2027/28, subject to management implementing all recommendations and no adverse findings emerging.
findings.matters: Four years without audit assurance over financial statements creates fundamental uncertainty over the council's financial position and control environment that directly affects lender credit assessment.
findings.figures: Four consecutive years of disclaimed opinions (2021/22–2024/25); backstop dates: 31 January 2027 for 2025/26 accounts
findings.quote: Disclaimed opinions were issued by the predecessor auditor for 2021/22 and 2022/23 and by Azets in 2023/24 and 2024/25. Following the publication of LARRIGs 01 to 06 we have developed an overarching strategy for building back assurance for the Council, with the aim of recovering assurance by 31 March 2028.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Annual Governance Statement 2025/26
findings.headline: Two audit areas received Limited Assurance: Old River Lane and Homelessness
findings.detail: Of 23 audits in 2025/26, nine received Substantial Assurance, eight Reasonable, and two Limited Assurance. The two Limited Assurance findings were for Old River Lane and Homelessness. Internal audit concluded these did not materially impact the overall opinion as findings were specific to individual areas rather than suggesting wider control issues.
findings.matters: Limited Assurance indicates control weaknesses in specific areas. While deemed non-material by internal audit, a lender would need to understand whether these issues affect services or assets material to the council's operations or finances.
findings.figures: 2 Limited Assurance out of 23 audits; 9 Substantial, 8 Reasonable, 4 advisory
findings.quote: In respect of the two audits receiving Limited assurance (Old River Lane & Homelessness), we concluded that this did not materially impact on our overall opinion as the related audit findings were specific to the individual area subject to audit, as opposed to suggesting wider control issues across the Council as a whole.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Annual Governance Statement 2025/26
findings.headline: Capital programme historically experienced slippage; management has strengthened oversight but scale is reducing
findings.detail: External auditors recommended strengthening capital programme management and forecasting due to historical slippage. Management has responded by providing more robust oversight through the Asset Management Group. However, the capital programme is now reducing in scale, which management notes 'should support improved deliverability'.
findings.matters: Capital programme slippage indicates project delivery management issues. The fact that scale is reducing suggests either a strategic shift or pragmatic recognition of delivery capacity constraints.
findings.figures: Capital programme reducing in scale going forward
findings.quote: More robust challenge and oversight of capital planning, profiling and delivery is being provided through the officer Asset Management Group. It is also noted that the capital programme is reducing in scale going forward, which should support improved deliverability and more realistic forecasting.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Annual Governance Statement 2025/26
findings.headline: BEAM project flagged as key exception requiring contingency pending business plan review
findings.detail: While the council is reducing reliance on reserves for revenue spending, BEAM is identified as 'the key exception'. A contingency remains in place pending the outcome of a business plan review. The statement does not provide detail on what BEAM is or why it requires ongoing contingency.
findings.matters: A named contingency on an identified project signals financial or delivery risk that a lender would want to understand in detail.
findings.figures: BEAM noted as outlier to otherwise improving financial management position
findings.quote: BEAM remains the key exception, with a contingency in place pending the outcome of the business plan review.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Annual Governance Statement 2025/26
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation will place additional demands on capacity and skills, with risk of losing key staff
findings.detail: External auditors flag that the council must assess whether it has necessary skills and capacity to support Local Government Reorganisation and identify gaps. Management acknowledges that LGR will place additional demands and may increase risk of losing key staff and corporate knowledge. Multiple recommendations emphasise ensuring financial decisions support the future unitary council and maintaining financial resilience through transition.
findings.matters: A lender needs assurance that the council will maintain strong financial governance, reporting capability, and senior staff continuity through local government reorganisation, particularly given the concurrent finance team restructuring.
findings.figures: MTFP extends to 2028/29; reorganisation occurring during this planning period
findings.quote: Management recognises that LGR will place additional demands on capacity and skills and may increase the risk of losing key staff and corporate knowledge. Skills and capacity are being reviewed to identify any gaps, with mitigating actions such as training or temporary support considered where required.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Annual Governance Statement 2025/26
findings.headline: Finance team restructure underway following capacity constraints that delayed accounts
findings.detail: The council approved a restructure of the finance team on 10 February 2026 following a review. Recruitment to vacant posts is progressing, with agency staff providing interim support. Quality assurance improvements include CFO review of draft accounts and weekly oversight meetings. Significantly, the 2024/25 accounts were completed on time 'for the first time in a number of years', indicating prior reporting delays were material.
findings.matters: Finance team capacity directly affects timeliness and quality of financial reporting. Prior delays in accounts completion are a red flag for lenders and the council's own finance director.
findings.figures: Restructure approved 10 February 2026; 2024/25 accounts completed within government timescales 'for the first time in a number of years'
findings.quote: Following a review of the team and service, a proposed restructure was presented to Leadership Team and approved on 10 February. Work is now progressing on recruitment to a number of vacant posts. In the interim, agency staff are supporting where necessary to ensure sufficient capacity within the team

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Corporate Risk Register Q4 2025/26
findings.headline: Asset disposal programme being used to pay down debt in response to funding pressures
findings.detail: The council has approved asset disposals with the explicit purpose of realising capital receipts to pay down debt. This sits alongside reductions in non-essential capital expenditure. The asset disposal programme is described as 'continuing', indicating this is an active ongoing strategy.
findings.matters: Using one-off capital receipts to reduce debt signals ongoing revenue pressure and reduces future financial flexibility when assets are exhausted.
findings.figures: No specific asset values or debt amounts disclosed
findings.quote: Non‑essential capital expenditure has been reduced, and asset disposals have been approved to realise capital receipts that will be used to pay down debt.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Corporate Risk Register Q4 2025/26
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creating one-off costs and transition disruption with significant uncertainty on timelines
findings.detail: LGR is classified as a new risk that places significant demands on capacity and may lead to additional one-off costs, service disruption, loss of key staff, and weakened financial resilience. Initial provision for one-off costs has been included in the MTFP, but significant uncertainty remains regarding implementation timelines and final structure. Council is monitoring national policy developments but lacks clarity on when and how the reorganisation will conclude.
findings.matters: Uncertainty on LGR timelines affects medium-term financial forecasting and risk of unexpected costs or service disruption during the transition period represents near-term financial exposure.
findings.figures: Initial provision for one-off costs included in Medium Term Financial Plan (no amount specified)
findings.quote: This may lead to additional one-off costs, disruption to service delivery, loss of key staff, reduced organisational focus on current priorities, and weakened financial resilience during the transition period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Corporate Risk Register Q4 2025/26
findings.headline: Section 114 notice threatened if expenditure continues to exceed funding
findings.detail: The council faces continued reductions in external funding combined with increasing service demand and inflationary pressures that could trigger a Section 114 notice from the s.151 Officer. This would require Commissioner appointment and trigger a formal public interest report. The council is actively seeking CIPFA support ahead of reaching this threshold to strengthen financial oversight. Asset disposals have been approved specifically to pay down debt, and non-essential capital expenditure has been reduced.
findings.matters: A Section 114 notice represents formal inability to balance the budget and is a core indicator of financial distress for lenders to local government.
findings.figures: No specific deficit figures disclosed; council is managing to what it calls 'real-terms reductions' in funding
findings.quote: Expenditure exceeds the resources available to the Council, caused by continued reductions in external funding, increasing service demand, and inflationary pressures, which could lead to the s.151 Officer issuing a Section 114(3) notice

findings.paper_title: Strategic Risk Register Quarter 4 2025/26
findings.headline: New corporate risk added for Local Government Reorganisation with potential for additional one-off costs
findings.detail: East Herts has added Risk 10 to the corporate register to capture financial, governance and service delivery uncertainties from potential local government reorganisation. The council explicitly identifies risks of additional one-off costs, organisational capacity pressure, and service delivery disruption during any transition period.
findings.matters: Lenders need visibility of potential material costs and organisational capacity constraints that could impact the council's financial position and service resilience
findings.figures: None specified for this risk in the document
findings.quote: The risk captures the financial, governance and service delivery uncertainties associated with LGR, including the potential for additional one-off costs, pressure on organisational capacity, and disruption to service delivery during any transition period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix C - Capital outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Multiple capital projects reclassified to revenue treatment, affecting capital programme reporting.
findings.detail: Hertford Castle Grounds development and some UKSPF schemes have been switched from capital to revenue accounting during 2025/26. This changes how their performance is measured against the capital programme.
findings.matters: Reclassifications can mask capital programme performance and affect comparability year-on-year.
findings.figures: Castle Grounds (270k), UKSPF Various (290k) moved to revenue treatment
findings.quote: All expenditurefor 2025/26 now treated as revenue.

findings.paper_title: Appendix C - Capital outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Hertford Theatre S278 outstanding works of £81k remain uncosted.
findings.detail: The council notes £81k of committed Section 278 infrastructure works that are outstanding and not yet invoiced. Costs are unknown but the council says they should stay within budget.
findings.matters: Unpriced committed expenditure creates cost uncertainty on a live project and affects year-end position.
findings.figures: Outstanding S278 works £81k
findings.quote: Outstanding S278 works (£81k). Figures not yet known but should still be within budget.

findings.paper_title: Appendix C - Capital outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Buntingford depot EV infrastructure planning application rejected; alternatives being sought.
findings.detail: The planned structural changes at Amwell as part of the depot EV infrastructure work failed planning. The council is now pursuing unspecified alternative opportunities, introducing uncertainty and likely delay.
findings.matters: Failed planning and need for alternatives signals project risk, cost pressure (alternatives may be more expensive), and delivery delay.
findings.figures: Additional £10k contingency was spent at Buntingford; Amwell alternative still undefined
findings.quote: Planning application for structural changes at Amwell was unsuccessful. Officers to seek alternatives opportunities.

findings.paper_title: Appendix C - Capital outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: BEAM website replacement went £9k over budget despite delivery.
findings.detail: The new website was launched in early February 2026 but exceeded its £51k budget. This is an explicit cost overrun on a completed project.
findings.matters: Indicates cost control issues on capital projects, which affects predictability of future scheme costs.
findings.figures: Budget £51k, Outturn £51k plus £9k over
findings.quote: Outturn is £9k over budget.

findings.paper_title: Appendix C - Capital outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Capital programme delivered only 72% of revised budget, with £3.3m underspent and £1.1m carried forward.
findings.detail: The revised budget was £11.925m; outturn was £8.628m, leaving £3.297m unspent. An additional £1.142m is carried into 2026/27. The shortfall represents material slippage across multiple project categories.
findings.matters: Large underspends raise questions about delivery capability, project planning, and the council's ability to execute its capital strategy on schedule.
findings.figures: Budget £11,925k, Outturn £8,628k, Variance (£3,297k), Carry Forward £1,142k
findings.quote: Current Capital Programme Budget Total 11,925 8,628 (3,297) 1,142

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Revenue outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Council drew an additional £1,196k from earmarked reserves beyond budget to balance the outturn
findings.detail: The budget assumed using £164k of earmarked reserves to balance the position. Actual usage was £1,360k — an additional £1,196k drawdown not provided for. This represents a one-off consumption of accumulated reserves to mask an underlying operating deficit.
findings.matters: Using reserves to fund operating expenditure is unsustainable and reduces financial flexibility for future years. When combined with the Net Cost of Services overspend of £2,405k, it shows the council's underlying position is worse than the headline year-end surplus suggests.
findings.figures: Budgeted reserve use £164k, actual use £1,360k, unbudgeted drawdown £1,196k
findings.quote: Contributions from Earmarked Reserves (164) (1,360) (1,196) (164) - (1,196)

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Revenue outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Unforecasted property fund loss of £448k in the final quarter
findings.detail: The outturn shows a loss on property funds of £448k that does not appear in any Q3 forecast line. This was entirely a fourth-quarter movement, suggesting either sudden investment losses or a revaluation that was not anticipated.
findings.matters: Unforecasted investment losses indicate either inadequate investment oversight or unexpected market deterioration affecting the council's capital portfolio. This erodes reserves and raises questions about asset management.
findings.figures: £448k loss entirely unbudgeted and unforecasted
findings.quote: (Gain)/Loss on Property Funds - 448 448 - - 448

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Revenue outturn 2025/26
findings.headline: Communities service overspend of £517k deteriorated sharply in quarter 4 with an additional £3.3m emerging between Q3 forecast and year-end
findings.detail: Communities had a revised budget of £5,479k and spent £5,996k (£517k overspend). At Q3, the same service was forecast at only £2,644k with an expected underspend of £2,835k. The position deteriorated by £3,352k between Q3 and outturn — the largest quarterly variance in the entire budget table. This represents uncontrolled spending in a major service area.
findings.matters: This scale of uncontrolled spending, combined with such dramatic forecast deterioration, indicates either serious cost control failure or an unexpected issue requiring emergency spending. Lenders need to understand what happened and whether it is one-off or systemic.
findings.figures: Revised budget £5,479k, outturn £5,996k, overspend £517k, Q3 forecast £2,644k, movement from Q3 £3,352k

findings.paper_title: External Auditors Audit Plan 2025/26
findings.headline: Audit and finance team capacity risk for significant 'build back work' needed to complete the 2025/26 audit
findings.detail: The audit plan explicitly identifies that both the external audit team and the council's finance team face capacity constraints in delivering the significant amount of build back work required to gain assurance on the accounts. This work is necessary to meet the statutory audit completion deadline of 31 January 2027.
findings.matters: Capacity limitations in the finance team performing remedial accounting work could delay audit completion, delay the audit opinion, and may signal underlying control or data integrity issues in the financial systems.
findings.figures: Statutory audit backstop date: 31 January 2027; audit fee: £185,917
findings.quote: The main risk to the delivery of the audit plan, and receiving an audit opinion by the back stop date is the capacity of both the audit team and finance team to deliver the significant amount of build back work required to gain assurance on the councils accounts.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Outturn 2025/26 and Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26
findings.headline: Lothbury Property Fund investment realized a £448K loss, partially offset by reserve usage
findings.detail: The council held an investment in the Lothbury Property Fund which produced a £448K loss. This loss was funded from reserve drawdowns and higher-than-expected investment income. The final redemption was received in May 2026. This represents a realized loss on an investment holding.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand the council's investment strategy and the risks it carries. A property fund loss suggests exposure to asset price volatility, and the reserves had to absorb the impact.
findings.figures: £448K loss on Lothbury Property Fund; final redemption received May 2026
findings.quote: A £448K loss on the Lothbury Property Fund, which was partially funded through reserve usage and the overachievement of investment income. The final redemption in relation to this property fund was received in May 2026, the £448k loss represents the final position on this fund.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Outturn 2025/26 and Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26
findings.headline: Parking service overspent by £348K with cleansing contract pressures marked for ongoing review
findings.detail: Parking overspent by £348K, attributed to business rates pressure (resolved for 2026/27) and a cleansing contract under review. The paper indicates that options for managing ongoing pressure are still being considered, suggesting the contract issue is not yet closed.
findings.matters: An unresolved contract issue in a utility service suggests operational management challenges. A lender would want clarity on the path to resolution and the ongoing financial exposure.
findings.figures: £348K overspend in Parking
findings.quote: £348K overspend in Parking, driven by higher business rates pressure, which has been resolved for 2026/27, and the cleansing contract which is under review and options to be considered for managing ongoing pressure.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Outturn 2025/26 and Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26
findings.headline: Capital programme underspend of £3.297M, with £2.155M deemed unrecoverable after budget reset in 2026/27 planning
findings.detail: The capital programme spent £8.628M against a budget of £11.925M. Post-year-end review concluded that two-thirds of the underspend (£2.155M) should not be carried forward, with significant budget resets on BEAM (£800K not rolled forward), ICT projects (£338K), and transformation programmes (£500K). This represents de-scoping rather than genuine slippage.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand why originally-approved capital plans were reset and why budgets for BEAM, ICT, and transformation were deemed to have been over-scoped. This may reflect financial constraints or delivery challenges.
findings.figures: £11.925M budget vs £8.628M outturn (£3.297M variance); £2.155M of underspend not carried forward; BEAM £800K, ICT £338K, other programmes £500K reset
findings.quote: Of the £3.297m underspend, approximately two-thirds (£2.155m) will not be carried forward to 2026/27, following a detailed review of budget requirements... The capital budgets for investment in BEAM, Depot Upgrades and Pinehurst Community Hall were reviewed as part of the 2026/27 budget setting process and reset to the required level, as a result, £800k of the 2025/26 underspends is not required to be carried forward.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Outturn 2025/26 and Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26
findings.headline: Earmarked reserves depleted by £2.038M in a single year to cover operational costs and one-off pressures
findings.detail: The council drew down £2.038M from earmarked reserves in 2025/26, including £986K for normal service costs (waste contract mobilisation, LG reorganisation, redundancies, housing benefits volatility, grounds maintenance), £678K to cover the revenue overspend itself, £240K for the Lothbury Property Fund loss, and £133K to smooth business rates collection issues. Total usable reserves fell from £21.340M to £19.302M.
findings.matters: Reserve depletion at this rate (10% in one year) is a concern for a lender, particularly when it includes recurring operational costs like grounds maintenance volatility and housing benefits volatility alongside one-off items.
findings.figures: £2.038M net transfer from earmarked reserves; total usable reserves fell from £21.340M to £19.302M
findings.quote: In 2025/26, a net £2.038M was transferred from the Council's Earmarked Reserves, with the main areas of reserve usage being: £986K to fund expenditure within the Net Cost of Services, including mobilisation costs of the new waste contract, costs associated with Local Government reorganisation, redundancies, volatility in the housing benefits budget and increased costs against the grounds maintenance contract; £678K to fund the 2025/26 revenue overspend

findings.paper_title: Provisional Outturn 2025/26 and Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26
findings.headline: BEAM service overspent by £1.167M, with the overspend worsening by £709K between Q3 and outturn
findings.detail: The council's BEAM service (which appears to be an operational/leisure service) delivered a £1.167M net overspend driven by lower income and higher staffing and operating costs. This overspend deteriorated significantly in the final quarter. The paper provides no confidence that this will be resolved.
findings.matters: A material overspend in a single service, deteriorating through the year, suggests either structural cost issues or revenue forecasting problems. A lender would want to understand whether this service is sustainable and whether the council has a recovery plan.
findings.figures: £1.167M overspend on BEAM; £709K adverse movement from Q3
findings.quote: £1.167M net overspend on BEAM (a £709K adverse movement from quarter 3) reflecting lower income and higher staffing and operating costs.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Outturn 2025/26 and Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26
findings.headline: Revenue budget overran by £678K, forcing use of general reserve to balance the year
findings.detail: The council's original budget anticipated a £6K underspend but the year closed with a £678K overspend. The Director for Finance approved funding this from the general reserve. The movement from Q3 forecast (£505K projected overspend) to outturn (£678K) represents £172K of deterioration, primarily in services and corporate budgets.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether this reflects temporary pressures or structural issues in the council's budget management and forecasting. The size and late emergence of the overspend suggests forecasting difficulty.
findings.figures: £678K overspend against 2025/26 budget; Q3 forecast £505K overspend
findings.quote: An overspend of £678K is reported against the 2025/26 revenue budget. In line with the Council's financial procedure rules the Director for Finance, Risk & Performance has approved that the overspend be funded from the general reserve.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2025/26 Mid-Year Review
findings.headline: Actual borrowing remains significantly above prudent benchmark level, with paper explicitly warning this approach carries higher risk
findings.detail: The council's actual borrowing of £64.5m at 31 March 2025 is more than double the calculated liability benchmark of £30.2m. Forecast borrowing at 31 March 2026 is projected at £68.0m against a benchmark of £53.5m. The paper explicitly acknowledges: 'Whilst borrowing may be above the liability benchmark, strategies involving borrowing which is significantly above the liability benchmark carry higher risk.'
findings.matters: Borrowing significantly above the prudent benchmark indicates the council holds more debt than the 'lowest risk level' suggests is necessary, limiting financial flexibility and increasing exposure to refinancing risk.
findings.figures: Borrowing: £64.5m vs benchmark £30.2m (31.3.25); forecast: £68.0m vs benchmark £53.5m (31.3.26)
findings.quote: Whilst borrowing may be above the liability benchmark, strategies involving borrowing which is significantly above the liability benchmark carry higher risk.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2025/26 Mid-Year Review
findings.headline: Legacy long-term debt locked at 8.875% for 30 years cannot be refinanced despite current market rates around 5.98%
findings.detail: The council holds £1.5m borrowed from PWLB at 8.875% fixed for 30 years. This loan cannot be restructured because gilt yields have not fallen sufficiently to create a discount (i.e., refinancing would cost more than the outstanding liability). The council remains locked into rates significantly above current market levels.
findings.matters: This legacy debt obligation represents a material above-market cost that will persist for three decades with no refinancing opportunity, materially increasing long-term debt servicing costs.
findings.figures: Legacy PWLB loan: £1.5m at 8.875% for 30 years; current 30-year rate 5.98%
findings.quote: Unfortunately, due to the high-interest rate East Herts is locked into we are not yet in a discounted but are constantly reviewing this position with our advisors Arlingclose.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2025/26 Mid-Year Review
findings.headline: Council keeping most borrowing short-term and actively seeking alternative funding sources, indicating unease with current PWLB rates
findings.detail: Rather than locking in long-term borrowing at current PWLB rates (10-year: 5.53%), the council is deliberately maintaining most borrowing on a short-term basis. It is actively pursuing alternative funding sources below gilt yields plus 0.80% as it believes PWLB rates may fall.
findings.matters: The council's strategy to avoid long-term PWLB borrowing suggests concern about current rate levels and future rate volatility, and indicates it may face pressure to refinance short-term debt at potentially higher rates if alternatives do not materialise.
findings.figures: PWLB 10-year certainty rate: 5.53% at 30.9.25; short-term borrowing from local authorities: 4.0% to 4.5%
findings.quote: The Authority is still opting to keep most borrowing short term, waiting for the longer term PWLB certainty rate to reduce. There remains a strong argument for diversifying funding sources, particularly if rates can be achieved on alternatives which are below gilt yields + 0.80%.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2025/26 Mid-Year Review
findings.headline: Strategic property fund investments being wound down after underperforming, requiring use of reserves to absorb losses
findings.detail: Two externally managed property pooled funds are being wound down (one already returned, the second completing by year-end). The authority is using its interest equalisation reserve to mitigate losses on the principal value of these investments. The council has decided to exit pooled fund investments entirely, with no plans for future similar investments.
findings.matters: Strategic investments designed to boost returns have underperformed expectations and necessitated reserve draw-downs to absorb principal losses. This signals the council's past investment strategy did not deliver, limiting future investment income.
findings.figures: Property funds were £12.8m at 31.3.25, reduced to £2.6m at 30.9.25
findings.quote: The Authority is using its interest equalisation reserve to mitigate any losses on principal value, from the two property funds, that we held.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2025/26 Mid-Year Review
findings.headline: Balance sheet resources forecast to fall 45% in one year while capital needs grow, driving structural increase in borrowing
findings.detail: Liquid financial resources are forecast to decline from £36.6m to £20.0m by year-end (31 March 2026), a £16.6m reduction. This is driven by large capital expenditures on waste vehicles, bins, and parish precepts, combined with the return of property fund investments. Meanwhile, the Capital Financing Requirement is rising from £61.8m to £68.5m, requiring additional borrowing to fund capital programmes.
findings.matters: Rapid depletion of liquid reserves while capital spending accelerates creates cash flow pressure and reduces the council's financial flexibility. A lender needs to understand the scale and duration of this capital programme.
findings.quote: Although property funds have been returned, investment levels, as at 30.09.25 have still reduced due to large expenditure items e.g. waste vehicles and bins, parish precepts.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Pay award provisioned at 4% but dependent on national negotiations; actual cost unknown
findings.detail: The budget assumes a 4% pay award for 2026/27 (increased from 3% assumption). The council notes the actual award is 'subject to national NJC negotiations' and is not yet settled. With c.800-1000 staff, a 1% variance is material. This is flagged as a budget pressure of £170k.
findings.matters: Pay is the largest cost base for councils. If the national award exceeds 4%, the council has limited headroom to absorb it. This is a category of cost the council does not control.
findings.figures: Pay award budget: £170k at 4%; assumes NJC settlement not finalised
findings.quote: The pay award projection for 2026/27 has been increased from 3% to 4% to reflect the 'higher for longer' position on inflation, ensuring the Council's budget remains resilient against ongoing wage pressures.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Business rates funding still provisional; settlement figures based on assumptions not actual data
findings.detail: The Baseline Funding Level (£2.657m) and tariff payment (£25.743m) are provisional estimates. Actual business rates data will not be received until January 2026 (NNDR1) and summer 2026 (bespoke data collection). Any material variance will affect the 2027/28 settlement. This is a live risk for the current budget year.
findings.matters: The council's 2026/27 budget is built on estimated business rates data, not final. If actual rates fall significantly—due to appeals, bad debts, or economic deterioration—the adjustment comes out of the 2027/28 settlement, creating future-year pressure.
findings.figures: Baseline Funding Level £2.657m; tariff £25.743m (both provisional)
findings.quote: Until the actual data is received—through the NNDR1 return in January 2026 and a bespoke data collection in summer 2026—the settlement figures are based on estimates. Once the true position is known, the Baseline Funding Level and tariff will be adjusted accordingly

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: General fund balance held flat at £3.854m while earmarked reserves decline from £17.3m to £13.7m
findings.detail: Total usable reserves are forecast to fall from £21.2m (2024/25) to £17.5m (2027/28). While the general fund balance is protected, earmarked reserves are being drawn down to fund planned commitments. By 2027/28, £3.3m of reserves have been spent or allocated.
findings.matters: A declining reserve position over a four-year horizon, even with the general fund maintained, indicates the council is consuming reserves to meet current spending. This is not sustainable indefinitely and signals tightening financial headroom.
findings.figures: Total usable reserves: £21.2m → £17.5m; earmarked reserves £17.3m → £13.7m
findings.quote: The projected balance of earmarked reserves is estimated to be £14.997 million by the end of March 2026 and £14.342 million by the end of March 2027, reflecting planned utilisation for approved commitments.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation costs are provisioned at £1m but carry execution risk
findings.detail: The council has allocated £1m over two years (£250k revenue, £250k reserves annually) for LGR implementation and a further £636k reserve set aside for potential pension strain or redundancy costs. The document notes costs 'are not yet fully understood' and a £203k contingency exists for the BEAM service specifically, suggesting known unknowns.
findings.matters: LGR is a structural event with costs that could exceed provision. Pension strain alone from restructuring can be material. A lender needs to know that the council is going through a major governance transition with estimated but uncertain costs.
findings.figures: £1m LGR funding over 2 years; £636k reserve provision for pension/redundancy; £203k BEAM contingency
findings.quote: It is anticipated that there will be further one-off costs associated with the implementation of LGR, including pension strain. The proposal is to provide an initial £1 million of funding over two years (2026/27 and 2027/28)

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: One-off pension fund benefit of £985k masks structural cost pressures
findings.detail: The triennial pension fund valuation improved to 107.3% funding (from 101.6%), allowing the primary rate to drop by £348k and secondary rate to cease with £637k saving. This is a one-time benefit that will not recur at the 2028 revaluation. Operating pressures of £706k were covered largely by this non-recurring pension outcome.
findings.matters: The council's balance sheet relies on a one-off pension gain that will not repeat. If the next triennial valuation (2028) moves unfavourably—quite possible with market volatility—the council has no buffer and no new savings identified to cover the hit.
findings.figures: Primary rate saving £348k; secondary rate cessation £637k
findings.quote: The outcome of the 2025 triennial valuation has a significant positive impact on the Council's financial position for 2026/27 and across the MTFP. The reduction in the primary employer contribution rate from 19.8% in 2025/26 to 17.1% from 2026/27 onwards—translates into a saving of £348,000 in 2026/27, with similar savings projected for subsequent years.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Parking income increase of £277k—13% of total identified savings—faced significant public consultation pushback
findings.detail: The council received 'a significant volume of responses' to parking tariff increases, with 'particularly strong feedback' opposing the 3.8% average increase in rural areas. The council partially backed down, keeping weekday charges unchanged in three towns but still forecasting the £277k saving. This income is central to the budget but politically fragile.
findings.matters: If the council has to reverse parking increases due to political pressure or economic circumstances, it loses the largest single identified income item (£277k out of £1,596k savings). The budget has little slack for this kind of slippage.
findings.figures: £277k parking income; 3.8% average increase planned
findings.quote: During the public consultation on these proposals, the Council received a significant volume of responses from residents and businesses. Many expressed concerns about the potential impact of increased charges on high street trade, accessibility for vulnerable groups, and congestion in residential areas.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Budget balance depends on maximum permitted council tax increases every year
findings.detail: The council is applying the 2.99% maximum permitted council tax increase for 2026/27 (Band D £207.03). The Options section makes clear that accepting a lower increase 'would create additional financial pressures in later years' and 'would result in a permanent loss of revenue'. The budget cannot balance without this lever being pulled annually.
findings.matters: Council tax is politically sensitive and there are limits to how high it can go before residents revolt or electoral consequences follow. If the council cannot deliver the assumed increases, the budget fails. The document reveals this as a structural dependency, not a choice.
findings.figures: 2.99% increase assumed; Band D £207.03
findings.quote: Any decision to reduce council tax, limit growth, or hold back on increases to fees and charges would create additional financial pressures in later years of the MTFP or result in increased budget monitoring challenges for 2026/27 and beyond.

findings.paper_title: Budget 2026-2031 & Medium Term Financial Plan 2026-2031
findings.headline: Core grant funding is declining 14% while council tax bears the gap
findings.detail: Core Spending Power including council tax rises 5.8% to £21.8m, but excluding council tax it falls from £7.9m to £6.8m over the period—a 14% reduction. Revenue Support Grant alone falls from £4.274m to £3.041m by 2028/29. The council is becoming structurally dependent on council tax and fee income as government grant erodes.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether a council's funding is resilient. A 14% decline in grant income concentrated in a few years creates refinancing risk if the council needs to borrow or if council tax growth slows.
findings.figures: CSP excluding council tax: £7.9m (2024/25) → £6.8m (2028/29); RSG: £4.274m → £3.041m
findings.quote: However, when council tax is excluded, CSP falls from £7.9m to £6.8m, a reduction of 14%.

findings.paper_title: Appendix D Section 25 Statement of the CFO
findings.headline: The council's 2026/27 budget depends critically on completing the disposal of all Millstream company properties
findings.detail: The council describes receipts from the Millstream property disposal as critical to reducing its MRP and interest costs. The council operates a minimal capital programme funded by heavy asset disposals. If these sales do not proceed at projected prices, the budget will face a funding gap.
findings.matters: A lender needs assurance that material budget assumptions will be delivered. Branding disposals as 'critical' signals they are essential to budget balance, making execution risk a key factor in lending decisions.
findings.figures: Millstream company properties; receipts to reduce MRP and interest costs
findings.quote: These receipts are critical to reducing the Council's Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) and interest costs.

findings.paper_title: Appendix D Section 25 Statement of the CFO
findings.headline: The council's accounts are disclaimed, and the auditor has not yet formed an opinion on its financial position
findings.detail: East Herts has caught up on statements of accounts through 2024/25, but these accounts remain disclaimed. The council is working with auditors to gain further assurance and move toward unqualified opinions. A disclaimer means the auditor could not verify the fairness of the accounts.
findings.matters: A lender cannot independently verify the council's financial position, reserves, or asset values until accounts are unqualified. Disclaimed accounts are a red flag for financial instability or control weaknesses.
findings.figures: Accounts disclaimed through 2024/25
findings.quote: While these accounts are currently disclaimed, work is progressing with auditors to gain further assurance and move towards unqualified opinions.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy, Minimum Revenue Provision Policy and Treasury Strategy 2026/27
findings.headline: Council's cash balances are primarily drawn from reserves rather than operations
findings.detail: The treasury strategy states that cash balances largely derive from reserves, and emphasises that any loss of principal from invested reserves would impact the General Fund. This indicates the council is operating with minimal discretionary cash generation from normal operations.
findings.matters: Reliance on reserves for cash flow rather than operations indicates a council in financial stress; reserves depletion over time is unsustainable.
findings.figures: Cash balances largely derive from reserves
findings.quote: As cash balances largely derive from reserves, maintaining the security of invested sums is paramount, as any loss of principal would impact the General Fund.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy, Minimum Revenue Provision Policy and Treasury Strategy 2026/27
findings.headline: Council has reached borrowing capacity and cannot borrow beyond levels already committed
findings.detail: Despite currently meeting the debt-to-capital financing requirement test, the council explicitly states there is no capacity for additional borrowing beyond schemes already in the programme. This removes one route to funding if circumstances deteriorate.
findings.matters: Lenders need to know whether a council has financial flexibility to weather unexpected costs or revenue shortfalls; this council does not.
findings.figures: No additional borrowing capacity available
findings.quote: While the Council is currently compliant, there is no capacity for additional borrowing beyond the levels already proposed.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy, Minimum Revenue Provision Policy and Treasury Strategy 2026/27
findings.headline: Capital programme restricted to health and safety critical schemes only, with no discretionary projects through 2028/29
findings.detail: The council explicitly states it has very limited financial resources and will restrict the capital strategy for 2026/27 to 2028/29 to only schemes that are health and safety critical or essential to maintaining core business continuity. This signals a significant tightening of capital investment flexibility across a three-year horizon.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether a council can invest in infrastructure, service improvement or economic development, or whether it is in survival mode; this council cannot.
findings.figures: 2026/27 to 2028/29; health and safety critical or essential schemes only
findings.quote: Given the Council's very limited financial resources, the Capital Strategy for 2026/27 to 2028/29 will focus exclusively on schemes that are health and safety critical or essential to maintaining core business continuity. There is no scope for discretionary or aspirational projects within this period.

findings.paper_title: Strategic Risk register Quarter 3 Monitoring
findings.headline: Amwell depot planning delays are pushing climate adaptation risk higher and threatening scheduled flood resilience works
findings.detail: The council's climate change risk moved from B3 (Medium likelihood annually) to B4 (High likelihood monthly) in Q3 2025/26, specifically because planning permission for the Amwell depot redevelopment has been delayed beyond earlier projected timelines. The planning aspects of this redevelopment are directly linked to the council's ability to adapt its estate to increasing flood risk. Without planning approval, essential adaptation works cannot proceed on schedule.
findings.matters: Unfinished infrastructure adaptation and repeated delays in major capital projects signal execution risk and potentially worsening exposure to climate-related disruption
findings.figures: B3 (Q2) to B4 (Q3); B4 = Significant impact (£400,000 to £1m p.a.) and High likelihood (monthly)
findings.quote: This reflects the continued absence of planning permission for the Amwell depot site, despite earlier projected timelines. The planning aspects of the Amwell redevelopment are directly linked to our ability to adapt the estate to increasing flood risk associated with climate change.

findings.paper_title: Financial Management 2025/26 - Quarter 3 Forecast to year end
findings.headline: UKSPF projects facing September 2026 delivery deadline with £235k budget underspent this year
findings.detail: The council has added £400k UK Shared Prosperity Fund grant to the capital programme for new projects but is forecasting a £235k underspend on these schemes. All UKSPF spending is being carried forward to 2026/27 ahead of a September 2026 deadline, creating a tight delivery window.
findings.matters: External funding with fixed deadlines creates execution pressure. Failure to deliver by September 2026 risks losing grant funding and damaging the council's credibility with government.
findings.figures: £400k UKSPF grant added to capital programme; £235k underspend on UKSPF projects; deadline September 2026
findings.quote: As these projects are expected to be delivered in 2026/27, ahead of the UKSPF deadline of September 2026, it is proposed that this budget is carried forward.

findings.paper_title: Financial Management 2025/26 - Quarter 3 Forecast to year end
findings.headline: Capital programme carrying forward £1.114m of unspent budget to 2026/27
findings.detail: The council forecast a £2.505m underspend on a revised £11.885m capital budget. Of this, £1.114m is expected to carry forward to 2026/27, indicating project delivery delays across multiple schemes including BEAM (£81k), Old River Lane (£59k), ICT Rolling Programme, and UKSPF projects.
findings.matters: Deferred capital spend signals execution risk and project delivery challenges. It also creates uncertainty in 2026/27 spending commitments and may indicate resource or planning constraints.
findings.figures: £2.505m total underspend; £1.114m carry-forward proposed; UKSPF projects £235k underspend with September 2026 deadline
findings.quote: We now expect to spend £9.38 million this year, which is £2.505 million less than planned... it is currently expected to be carried forward... remains subject to change at year‑end.

findings.paper_title: Financial Management 2025/26 - Quarter 3 Forecast to year end
findings.headline: BEAM service income falling £191k short of target
findings.detail: Regeneration, Customer & Commercial – BEAM has an adverse movement of £191k since Q2 because income is not meeting the expected target. This is the second-largest driver of overspend and represents a demand or pricing issue.
findings.matters: Income underperformance is harder to recover mid-year than cost overspend. It signals either demand softness, pricing issues, or collection problems in a service the council is relying on for revenue.
findings.figures: £191k adverse movement in BEAM; contingency funds released to offset this
findings.quote: Regeneration, Customer & Commercial – BEAM: an adverse movement of £191k, driven by income not meeting the expected target.

findings.paper_title: Financial Management 2025/26 - Quarter 3 Forecast to year end
findings.headline: Planning service hit by £216k salary and agency cost pressure since Q2
findings.detail: Place – Planning has seen the largest adverse movement since Q2 at £216k, driven specifically by increased pressures from salary and agency costs. This is the largest single cost driver of the overall overspend and suggests ongoing staffing cost volatility.
findings.matters: Runaway agency and salary costs in a single service area indicate either pay/staffing policy issues or service demand spikes that cannot be absorbed. This is a common precursor to sustained overspend.
findings.figures: £216k adverse movement in Place – Planning
findings.quote: Place – Planning: an adverse movement of £216k, mainly due to increased pressures from salary and agency costs.

findings.paper_title: Financial Management 2025/26 - Quarter 3 Forecast to year end
findings.headline: Revenue overspend of £505k (2.5% of budget) forecast to year end
findings.detail: The council's net revenue budget is £20.134m. Based on spending to 31 December 2025, the Q3 forecast is for an overspend of £505k by year end. This represents a material variance that has not been resolved mid-year. The overspend persists despite some favourable movements in other areas.
findings.matters: A material unresolved overspend signals budget management issues and creates risk for reserve position. Lenders care whether the council controls its spending.
findings.figures: £505k overspend on £20.134m budget; Net Cost of Services overspend £906k partially offset by corporate budget underspend of £758k
findings.quote: Based on spending up to 31 December 2025, we are currently forecasting that we will overspend by £505,000 by the end of the financial year.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Audit Completion Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Finance team restructuring underway; audit delays caused by inability to provide requested information within planned timeframe
findings.detail: The Council is undertaking finance team restructuring to strengthen audit support capability. Planning work originally scheduled for December 2024–January 2025 could not be completed because required information and listings were not received. Planning was deferred to July–September 2025, compressing the fieldwork timeline.
findings.matters: Ongoing restructuring and delays in providing audit information suggest weakness in financial controls, documentation practices, and management capacity. Successful restructuring is critical to resolving the auditor's concerns and regaining audit assurance.
findings.figures: Planning originally scheduled Dec 2024–Jan 2025; actually completed July–Sep 2025
findings.quote: The Council is currently undergoing a finance team restructuring aimed at strengthening its ability to support the audit process... Planning work was originally scheduled for completion during the December-January 2024 period. However, we were unable to obtain the required information from the Council within that timeframe.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Audit Completion Report 2024-25
findings.headline: No assurance over opening balances and reserves across all major balance sheet items due to prior-year disclaimer cascade
findings.detail: Because 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24 accounts were all disclaimed, the auditor has no assurance over opening balances for any year, including critical items like pension liabilities, property valuations, and reserves. This cascading uncertainty makes it impossible to validate 2024/25 movements or closing balances with confidence.
findings.matters: Without assurance over opening balances, the auditor cannot confirm the accuracy of reported reserves, asset valuations, or pension liabilities. These are essential to understanding the Council's true financial position and sustainability.
findings.figures: Opening balances unaudited for 2021/22 through 2024/25; Other Comprehensive Income changed from £18,576k to £17,603k between comparative figures; total unusable reserves changed from £16,440k to £21,033k
findings.quote: Due to audit opinions on the prior years' financial statements being disclaimed, we have no assurance over the opening balances of the reserves and the balance sheet financial statement line items. This means we have no assurance on the movements in year and cannot gain sufficient audit evidence on the material accuracy of the financial statements at 31 March 2025.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Audit Completion Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Council debt at 106% of Capital Financing Requirement, indicating overextension with minimal financial headroom
findings.detail: The Council's total debt is 106% of its CFR, which exceeds the prudent benchmark of 100%. The auditor explicitly states this indicates the Council is 'overextended on its borrowing with minimal financial headroom.' This means the Council has borrowed beyond what its capital spending justifies and has little room to manage fluctuations.
findings.matters: An over-leveraged borrowing position limits the Council's financial flexibility and increases risk if revenues fall, interest rates rise, or capital schemes overrun. This directly affects the Council's ability to service debt and fund operations.
findings.figures: Debt to CFR ratio: 106% (prudent benchmark: below 100%)
findings.quote: the Council's position of 106% indicates it is overextended on its borrowing with minimal financial headroom

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Audit Completion Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Minimum Revenue Provision at 1.2% of Capital Financing Requirement, well below prudent benchmark of 2%
findings.detail: The Council's MRP charge for 2024/25 is only 1.2% of opening CFR, placing it below the level typically considered prudent for debt repayment. This indicates insufficient provision is being made to repay borrowing. The MRP is due to double in 2025/26 to £1.431m (2.3% of opening CFR), suggesting management recognises the prior year provision was inadequate.
findings.matters: Inadequate MRP provision means the Council is not setting aside sufficient resources to repay its debt, risking future cash flow problems and structural deficits as borrowing comes due.
findings.figures: MRP 2024/25: 1.2% of opening CFR; MRP 2025/26: £1.431m (2.3% of opening CFR); rising to £1.453m in 2026/27
findings.quote: The Council's MRP charge is only 1.2% of the opening CFR. This does not indicate that the 2024/25 MRP is incorrect; however, it does place the charge below the level typically considered prudent.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Audit Completion Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Auditor intends to disclaim opinion on 2024/25 accounts, cannot form view on financial statements
findings.detail: Due to backstop date constraints and inability to complete planned procedures, the auditor cannot express an opinion on whether the 2024/25 financial statements give a true and fair view. This follows disclaimed opinions on 2021/22, 2022/23, and 2023/24, meaning the Council's accounts have not received an unqualified audit opinion since 2020/21.
findings.matters: A disclaimer of opinion means lenders have no external assurance over the Council's financial position, assets, liabilities or reserves. This is the most serious type of audit outcome and signals fundamental uncertainty about the reliability of reported figures.
findings.figures: Backstop date 27 February 2026; prior year disclaimers on 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24
findings.quote: it is not possible for us to undertake sufficient work to support an unmodified audit opinion ahead of the backstop date of 27 February 2026. Undertaking work on balances that have not been subject to audit for several years necessarily means the audit on the current year balances takes longer than would ordinarily be the case... We therefore intend to disclaim our opinion.

findings.paper_title: Update on Statutory Recommendation from External Auditors and Finance Peer Review
findings.headline: Quality assurance processes for draft accounts only recently implemented and still being strengthened
findings.detail: Quality assurance processes for draft accounts have only recently started, with the new CFO reviewing recent accounts. Further improvements are being considered including formal review checks and weekly oversight meetings to ensure proper segregation of duties.
findings.matters: Formal quality assurance processes for accounts are fundamental controls; their recent implementation suggests controls were previously inadequate
findings.figures: New CFO has reviewed recent accounts
findings.quote: The quality assurance process for draft accounts has started, with recent accounts reviewed by the new CFO. A timetable for the next closedown is in place, and further improvements – such as formal review checks and weekly oversight meetings – are being considered to ensure proper segregation of duties and ongoing monitoring.

findings.paper_title: Update on Statutory Recommendation from External Auditors and Finance Peer Review
findings.headline: Finance team heavily reliant on specific individuals with workflow bottlenecks being reviewed
findings.detail: The council is reviewing its Finance Team structure to reduce reliance on specific individuals and address workflow bottlenecks. The review involves input from senior officers and benchmarking against similar authorities.
findings.matters: Over-reliance on specific individuals creates operational risk; if key staff leave, the finance function's effectiveness could be compromised
findings.figures: None specified
findings.quote: The Finance Team structure is being reviewed to reduce reliance on specific individuals and address bottlenecks to improve workflow, with input from senior officers and benchmarking against similar authorities.

findings.paper_title: Update on Statutory Recommendation from External Auditors and Finance Peer Review
findings.headline: External auditors issued statutory recommendations over financial governance and timely savings delivery
findings.detail: EY auditors issued statutory recommendations in April 2025 following audit of 2021/22 and 2022/23 accounts, citing concerns about financial governance and whether savings plans were being delivered on time. The council agreed to strengthen financial controls and improve reporting to Members.
findings.matters: Statutory recommendations from external auditors indicate the council had significant governance weaknesses that require formal correction and ongoing monitoring
findings.figures: Recommendations issued April 2025 following audit of 2021/22 and 2022/23 accounts
findings.quote: The external auditors, EY, issued a statutory recommendation in April 2025, which was subsequently presented to Audit & Governance and then to Full Council in May 2025. These recommendations arose from concerns identified during the audit of the 2021/22 and 2022/23 accounts, particularly around financial governance and timely delivery of savings plans.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024/25
findings.headline: Internal audit findings are not being addressed promptly, requiring CFO oversight and Leadership Team escalation
findings.detail: Auditors flagged that 'Council needs to ensure actions are taken to address weaknesses identified by Internal Audit on a timely basis' as an ongoing issue. The council's response includes regular CFO-auditor meetings, Leadership Team monthly focus on finance, and escalation to Operation Council where necessary.
findings.matters: Slow implementation of audit recommendations indicates weak governance culture and means control weaknesses persist longer than necessary, increasing operational and financial risk
findings.figures: No specific number of outstanding recommendations disclosed
findings.quote: Council needs to ensure actions are taken to address weaknesses identified by Internal Audit on a timely basis.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024/25
findings.headline: External auditors issued three formal statutory recommendations on finance function workflow, quality assurance, and team capacity
findings.detail: Auditors formally required the council to: (1) conduct comprehensive review of finance workflow to identify bottlenecks and redistribute workload; (2) implement thorough QA review of draft accounts with clear timelines and segregation of duties; (3) re-assess finance team roles and resources to restore timely financial reporting. These recommendations were only formally raised in April 2025, acknowledged as insufficient time for implementation.
findings.matters: Statutory recommendations indicate auditors have significant concerns about the finance function's capability to deliver compliant financial reporting; formal recommendations are escalated governance issues
findings.figures: Three statutory recommendations issued; acknowledged insufficient time for implementation as of March 2025
findings.quote: Conduct a comprehensive review of the finance function workflow to identify bottlenecks in the flow of information and the completion of key finance tasks. Use the findings to redefine roles and responsibilities within the finance team, ensuring an equitable distribution of workload and preventing any single individual from being overburdened.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024/25
findings.headline: The council is relying on reserve balancers to support the revenue budget, indicating structural financial pressure
findings.detail: External auditors recommended the council mitigate 'the further use of reserve balancers to support the revenue budget in the medium term.' The statement indicates this will be addressed in the Medium-Term Financial Plan, but the use of reserves to offset spending is a sign that the council is not balancing operations through savings or income alone.
findings.matters: Using reserves to support revenue budgets depletes financial flexibility and signals structural deficit; it limits the council's ability to respond to future shocks or invest in transformation
findings.figures: No specific reserve amounts disclosed in this extract; addressed through MTFP process planned for October
findings.quote: Mitigates the further use of reserve balancers to support the revenue budget in the medium term.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024/25
findings.headline: Finance team capacity constraints have impacted the council's ability to provide timely audit evidence and complete financial statements
findings.detail: The council acknowledges the finance team 'has experienced significant capacity issues, leading to delays in completing financial statements and supporting the external audit process.' To address this, an additional interim has been brought in and a structural review is underway following arrival of new S151 Officer in April 2025.
findings.matters: Insufficient finance team capacity prevents timely delivery of financial reports and audit evidence, creating reputational and compliance risk
findings.figures: New S151 Officer hired 1 April 2025; additional interim resource brought in
findings.quote: The finance team has experienced significant capacity issues, leading to delays in completing financial statements and supporting the external audit process. This has impacted on the Council's ability to provide timely, sufficient, and appropriate audit evidence to support the external audit.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024/25
findings.headline: Finance team has a single point of failure with over-reliance on one individual for critical financial tasks, creating risk to financial operations continuity
findings.detail: External auditors identified that a single person concentrates critical financial duties, creating substantial risk that errors will occur and operations will fail if that person is absent or departs. The council acknowledges this was a structural weakness and a new S151 Officer started 1 April 2025; a review of team structure is underway.
findings.matters: Dependence on a single individual for critical finance functions is a control failure that threatens the council's ability to produce reliable financial information and meet statutory obligations
findings.figures: New S151 Officer started 1 April 2025; review of team to be completed within first six months
findings.quote: The report by the External Auditors identifies a significant risk associated with the current structure of the finance team, specifically pointing out a single point of failure. This issue arises from the over-reliance on one individual for critical financial tasks and responsibilities.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024/25
findings.headline: East Hertfordshire has repeatedly failed to publish draft financial statements by statutory deadlines, with delays ranging from 16 to 29 months
findings.detail: The council published 2021/22 accounts 16 months late (December 2023 vs July 2022 deadline), 2022/23 accounts 29 months late (November 2024 vs May 2023 deadline), and 2023/24 accounts in April 2025. The statement claims 2024/25 was published on 27 June 2025 'in line with statutory deadline,' but this represents a multi-year systemic failure in financial closure.
findings.matters: Inability to publish financial statements on time is a core governance failure; it prevents stakeholders, auditors, and lenders from accessing reliable financial information when needed to make decisions
findings.figures: 2021/22 published 11 December 2023 (deadline 31 July 2022); 2022/23 published 6 November 2024 (deadline 31 May 2023); 2023/24 published 29 April 2025
findings.quote: The 2021/22 draft financial statements were published on 11 December 2023, significantly after the statutory deadline of 31 July 2022. The 2022/23 draft financial statements were not published until 6 November 2024, again missing the statutory deadline of 31 May 2023.
